metadata.title: Homemade Fig Jam
metadata.description: When it comes to homemade jam recipes, there are a variety of different selections that you can make. This recipe for Homemade Fig Jam is one of kind that goes great on toast or your favorite crackers. Easy to make, it is ready in minutes and can be preserved and saved for later. Join Dorothy from the RawFoodBlog and learn how to make this easy recipe.

nodes.plm_caption:
In the video a woman wearing a salmon-colored blouse is showing how to make a healthy smoothie. The video shows the ingredients needed, the person blending the ingredients, pouring into bowls, sprinkling spices in, and the finished product. In the background, there is a blue and greenish-colored wall, art prints, and pictures as well as a desk with electronics and a bookshelf.

The lighting is bright natural light coming in from an open window. The color scheme is blue and green and very calming and relaxing. There are also a few other colors such as yellow, pink, gray, beige and red. The room also has a cozy feel to it.

summary.brief: A woman in a salmon‑colored blouse makes quick homemade fig jam and serves it on raw kimchi crackers.
summary.detailed: The video opens with black screens displaying the www.favehealthyrecipes.com logo and the title “Fig Jam.” Dorothy from the Raw Food Blog then appears in a bright kitchen wearing a salmon‑colored blouse. She rinses fresh figs, removes their stems, and places three figs into a small bullet‑style blender. She adds the juice of half a lemon, a tablespoon of chia seeds that have been soaked in water for about ten minutes, a pinch of cinnamon and a few drops of stevia. She blends the mixture until it reaches a thick, jam‑like consistency, noting that a little water or apple juice could be added if it becomes too thick. After blending, she spoons the jam onto raw kimchi crackers and mentions other possible ways to enjoy it, such as with yogurt, banana, apple or fruit salad. The segment ends with a static slide showing the Fave Healthy Recipes logo and credit text.

action.detailed: Place fresh figs, lemon juice, soaked chia seeds, cinnamon and stevia into a small bullet blender, blend until the mixture thickens into jam, then spoon the jam onto raw kimchi crackers (or other toppings).
action.actor: A middle‑aged woman wearing a salmon‑colored blouse, identified as Dorothy from the Raw Food Blog

summary.brief: A woman prepares homemade fig jam from fresh figs.
summary.detailed: The clip opens with a brief graphic showing the website www.favehealthyrecipes.com and the title “Fig Jam.” It then cuts to a kitchen where a woman in a light‑colored blouse stands at a table covered with a yellow floral cloth. She washes fresh figs, removes their stems, and places three figs into a small stainless‑steel “bullet” container. She squeezes the juice of half a lemon over the figs, then adds a tablespoon of chia seeds that she has pre‑soaked in a little water. After that she incorporates a sweetener—stevia mixed with a pinch of cinnamon—and pours the mixture into a personal blender, blending until smooth. She mentions that if the jam looks too thick she could thin it with a splash of water or apple juice. The finished jam is shown ready to be poured into a container or served on crackers, yogurt, fruit, or kimchi crackers.

action.detailed: Combine fresh figs, lemon juice, soaked chia seeds, and a stevia‑cinnamon sweetener in a blender, blend to a thick jam consistency, and pour into a serving container.
action.actor: A woman in a light‑colored blouse (the video host)

In the background, we see a red item on a table and some unopened avocados.
The video starts with a person, we can't see his face, in a kitchen preparing a smoothie. The lady looks like she is in her kitchen in the middle of the day or early morning. We can see that there are a lot of ingredients inside of the blender as it is blended. She shows the camera the resulting smoothie. There are no other objects that are in the video besides what we've already talked about. The video is in English, but the first word is not correct. They say FAVEH (I think). The logo in the end has three icons inside of it. The icons are 1. A piece of food. 2. A white bowl of food. 3. A plate of food. The first is orange and red. The second is red. The third is green. summary.brief: A woman in a pink tank top mixes a dark ingredient, blends it into a thick jam, and tastes the result.
summary.detailed: The video shows a woman wearing a pink tank top standing at a kitchen table covered with an orange‑floral tablecloth. She holds a small red cup filled with a dark, powder‑like substance, scoops some of it with a spoon, adds a pinch of salt and stirs. She then pours the mixture into a clear blender, blends it until it becomes a dense, jam‑like paste, and pours the paste into two small red bowls. A piece of fruit is placed on top, she lifts a spoonful, tastes it, and smiles. The segment ends with the brand’s logo and promotional text on a black background.

You evaluate YouTube videos for a video-understanding benchmark.

You will be given an Action100M-style summary of one video: title, description,
a hierarchical GPT-written summary of the whole video, and a deduplicated list
of action labels extracted at multiple levels of the video.

Your job is to judge:

1) DOMAINS — does this video clearly belong to either of these target domains?
   - "kitchen": a person preparing food in a kitchen-like setting
     (cooking, baking, food prep — NOT eating reviews, NOT pet-food prep,
     NOT food-product unboxing, NOT restaurant vlogs).
   - "manipulation": a person performing hand-object manipulation tasks
     with clear physical goals: assembly/disassembly, repair, crafting,
     tool use, packing, sorting. The video must show clear procedural
     manipulation, NOT just incidental hand movement (e.g. a vlog where
     someone holds things while talking does NOT count).
   A video can match neither, one, or both. Be strict — when in doubt,
   say "neither".

2) NUM_DISTINCT_EVENTS — count the number of *semantically distinct*
   sub-events (procedural steps) you see in the action list. Merge
   paraphrases of the same step into one. Ignore generic narration steps
   like "speak to camera" or "display title".

3) IS_GOOD_CANDIDATE — true only if BOTH:
   - at least one target domain matches
   - num_distinct_events > 3 (the video shows a real multi-step procedure)

Always return strict JSON in the requested schema.
